hook.line: In the news, every cause has a mood. The flight is late, the café is full, the street is closed: someone is to thank, someone is to blame, or nobody is. Spanish chooses a different phrase for each.
hook.es: Gracias a Hernando, encontramos la carta.
hook.en: Thanks to Hernando, we found the letter.

examples.es: Gracias a la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
examples.en: Thanks to the rain, the plants are green.

examples.es: Por culpa de la lluvia, cancelaron el partido.
examples.en: Because of the rain, they called off the match.

examples.es: Debido a la lluvia, el vuelo está retrasado.
examples.en: Due to the rain, the flight is delayed.

examples.es: Gracias a ti conseguí el trabajo.
examples.en: Thanks to you, I got the job. (to a friend)

examples.es: Por culpa del ruido, no dormí nada.
examples.en: Because of the noise, I didn't sleep at all.

examples.es: Debido a un incendio, la calle está cerrada.
examples.en: Due to a fire, the street is closed.

examples.es: Gracias a que Mariana escribió el artículo, todos saben la verdad.
examples.en: Thanks to the fact that Mariana wrote the article, everyone knows the truth.

rule:
The three phrases fit the same slot. What changes is the mood.

*Gracias a*: a good result, someone to thank.
*Por culpa de*: a bad result, someone to blame.
*Debido a*: neutral, just the cause. It is formal and very common in news and announcements.

All three take a noun: *gracias a ti*, *por culpa del trancón*, *debido a la lluvia*. Remember *de* + *el* becomes *del*, and *a* + *el* becomes *al*.

Before a verb, add *que*: *gracias a que…*, *debido a que…*, *por culpa de que…*

The verb stays plain, since you are stating a fact. Never *gracias de* or *debido de*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *debido a* a formal causal preposition. The other two carry a judgement: good or bad.

readAndPick.es: Por culpa de la lluvia, cancelaron el partido.
options: Thanks to the rain, they called off the match.
Despite the rain, they called off the match.
It's the rain's fault they called off the match.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a Vale, el café está lleno.
options: Thanks to Vale, the café is full.
It's Vale's fault the café is full.
Despite Vale, the café is full.

readAndPick.es: Debido a un incendio, la calle está cerrada.
options: Thanks to a fire, the street is closed.
Due to a fire, the street is closed.
It's the fire's fault, but the street is open.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a ti conseguí el trabajo.
options: It's your fault I got the job.
I didn't get the job because of you.
Thanks to you, I got the job.

readAndPick.es: Por culpa del ruido, no dormí nada.
options: Because of the noise, I didn't sleep at all.
Thanks to the noise, I slept well.
Despite the noise, I slept all night.

readAndPick.es: Debido a la protesta, hay trancón.
options: The protest happens because of the traffic.
The protest is to blame for the traffic.
Due to the protest, there is a traffic jam.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a que Mariana escribió el artículo, todos saben la verdad.
options: Thanks to Mariana writing the article, everyone knows the truth.
Mariana wrote the article, but nobody knows the truth.
Mariana is to blame that everyone knows.

readAndPick.es: Por culpa de Altamira, tenemos un problema.
options: Thanks to Altamira, we have a problem.
Because of Altamira, we have a problem.
Altamira has a problem.

readAndPick.es: Debido a que hay una inundación, cerraron la escuela.
options: Because there's a flood, they closed the school.
Thanks to a flood, the school is open.
Because they closed the school, there is a flood.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *gracias a* or *por culpa de*, and type the whole sentence: *___ Vale, el café está lleno.* (Thanks to Vale, the café is full.)
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a Vale, el café está lleno.
yourTurn.why: A full café is good news, so you thank Vale: *gracias a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *gracias a* or *por culpa de*, and type the whole sentence: *___ ruido, no dormí nada.* (Because of the noise, I didn't sleep at all.)
yourTurn.answer: Por culpa del ruido, no dormí nada.
yourTurn.why: A bad night is bad news, so the noise gets the blame, and *de* + *el* becomes *del*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say as in the news, neutrally: Due to a fire, the street is closed.
yourTurn.answer: Debido a un incendio, la calle está cerrada.
accept: La calle está cerrada debido a un incendio.
yourTurn.why: Just stating a cause, without thanks or blame: *debido a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: Thanks to you, I got the job.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a ti conseguí el trabajo.
accept: Gracias a ti, conseguí el trabajo.
Conseguí el trabajo gracias a ti.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Because of Altamira, we have a problem.
yourTurn.answer: Por culpa de Altamira, tenemos un problema.
accept: Tenemos un problema por culpa de Altamira.
yourTurn.why: Altamira gets the blame: *por culpa de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it neutral and formal: *Por culpa de la inundación, cerraron la calle.* (Due to the flood, they closed the street.)
yourTurn.answer: Debido a la inundación, cerraron la calle.
yourTurn.why: Swap the blame for the neutral *debido a* and nothing else changes.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Thanks to the fact that Mariana wrote the article, everyone knows the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a que Mariana escribió el artículo, todos saben la verdad.
accept: Todos saben la verdad gracias a que Mariana escribió el artículo.
yourTurn.why: Before a whole clause with its own verb, add *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Gracias de la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
pitfalls.right: Gracias a la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. This one takes *a*, not *de*: *gracias a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Por culpa de la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
pitfalls.right: Gracias a la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
pitfalls.why: Green plants are good news, and *por culpa de* always sounds like blame.

pitfalls.wrong: Debido de la lluvia, el vuelo está retrasado.
pitfalls.right: Debido a la lluvia, el vuelo está retrasado.

pitfalls.wrong: Por culpa de el ruido, no dormí nada.
pitfalls.right: Por culpa del ruido, no dormí nada.

personal: Think of something good that happened this week and say who to thank with *gracias a…*, then something annoying with *por culpa de…*.
